sections.title: Local remediation, code points and UTF-8

keyTerms.definition: The number Unicode assigns to a character, an integer in [0, 0x10FFFF].
The fixed bridge that turns code points into bytes, using one to four bytes per code point.
Byte pair encoding. It starts from bytes or characters and repeatedly merges the most frequent neighboring pair.
The regex cut of text into chunks. BPE merges run inside each chunk only.
Tokens per word. Larger vocabularies buy lower fertility and pay more embedding parameters.
A fenced-off substring mapped to a reserved id. It never enters pair counting or merging.

recall.question: Why do modern tokenizers use subword units instead of whole words?
recall.answer: Whole words explode the vocabulary and leave an unknown-word hole. Subwords split rare words into reusable pieces, so every string decomposes into known pieces.

recall.question: What two phases make up BPE, and what decides the merge order?
recall.answer: Pair counting and merging. BPE counts adjacent pairs weighted by word frequency and merges the most frequent pair first. Encoding applies the learned merges greedily, left to right.

recall.question: What three invariants must a tokenizer roundtrip satisfy?
recall.answer: Decode(encode(s)) equals s for all valid strings. Encode is deterministic. Ids decode to the exact byte sequence consumed, with no silent normalization.
